newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates stay weak for Mideast/Japan.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates stay weak for Mideast/Japan.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates for 250,000 tonne Very Large Crude Carriers (VLCCs) plying Mideast/Japan routes were still sickly on Thursday while West Africa to UK/Cont numbers fell for Suezmaxes, shipbrokers said.

While vessels of around 300,000 tonnes were fixed eastwards from the Middle East in a steady trickle at between W45 and W50, brokers said VLCC rates for European routes were under pressure because of a surplus of vessels in the Middle East.
"It is tailing off and there is tonnage around looking for business," one broker said, adding that a 280,000 tonne requirement for a Mideast/Red Sea voyage had received 10 offers.
Mideast/Japan rates were assessed at around W65 for VLCCs and were unlikely to rise, with most Japanese commitments already covered into the New Year.
West African markets were calmer following an earlier flurry of million-barrel and two-million-barrel fixtures.
But rates for European destinations for Suezmaxes were weaker. "That has come off by about five points," one broker said, adding that a lack of enquiry was dampening sentiment.
Brokers assessed West Africa/Med rates at around W95 or lower, while they saw U.S. Gulf destinations worth above W90, and the USAC a couple of points higher than that.
Fuel oil rates appeared to be under pressure amid a relative lack of enquiry, especially from the Baltics.
One broker saw rates for 25,000 tonnes making inter UK/Cont voyages having slipped to about W190-195. "It could get worse before the weekend too."
Rates in the Med, however, were better supported as bad weather caused scattered delays and cancellations. Ships of 25,000 tonnes were assessed at around W200 for Cross-Med journeys.
